clue.text: Cache discovered in South-east Mediterranean island

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east
Crete is the large Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Someone finds a hoard of treasure on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cache' looks like a noun, a hoard, but here it is the verb: to hide something away.
explanation.definitionFit: To cache something is to hide it, which is what secreting it means.

clue.text: Pass the big gun an Irish dish

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a cannon is a large gun

explanation.surface: An instruction at table to hand over a big gun and an Irish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: COLCANNON is mashed potato mixed with cabbage or kale, a traditional Irish dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Colcannon is a traditional Irish recipe of mashed potato with cabbage.

clue.text: A woman will take nothing back in the main

indicators.note: the sea takes something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the main is an old poetic name for the open sea

indicators.note: back tells us the word for nothing is read the other way round

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A woman drops something worthless back into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old literary term for the open sea; 'back' reverses the word for nothing and 'will take' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Selina is a girl's given name, so it fits a clue asking for a woman.

clue.text: Such people may find ant-bites turn nasty

indicators.note: the letters turn, changing into a new, nasty arrangement

explanation.surface: Travellers in the Himalayas suffer ant bites that become infected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn nasty' shuffles the letters of ANT-BITES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tibetans are a nation of people from the Himalayan region of Tibet; 'such people' points to the anagram as a description.

clue.text: Recovered or went round the bend!

definitions.meaning: got better, past the worst of an illness or crisis
literally drove or walked around a street corner, with a joke on going mad

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means began to recover, while literally it means went around a corner in the road.

clue.text: By no means finished trading

parts.note: read as having no money, so a business is forced to stop trading, not still going strong

explanation.definitionFit: A firm with no funds left is insolvent and must stop doing business.

clue.text: Least well-organised accounts

indicators.note: the letters are organised into a new tidy order

explanation.surface: A complaint about the most poorly kept books of accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories are accounts of events, so the plural noun fits.

clue.text: Person refusing to take advantage of French prohibitionist?

definitions.text: Person refusing to take advantage of French prohibitionist?

parts.words: Person refusing to take advantage of French prohibitionist?
parts.note: one who declines to use something; whimsically also someone who keeps saying the French word for no, a prohibition

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains from using a facility, read whimsically as one who uses the French refusal word.

clue.text: Previously carried around a couple of notes

indicators.note: around tells us one word wraps the other

parts.note: bore is the past tense of bear, to carry
E and F are two notes of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having once carried a couple of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests money, but these are musical notes, E and F.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier in time; a synonym for formerly.

clue.text: Foul-smelling fish causing some bitterness

parts.note: rank means having a strong unpleasant smell
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A stinking fish makes someone resentful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles causes lasting resentment.

clue.text: A bit can fit — or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise asks for the letters arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A small piece might or might not slot in.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction is a small part or portion of something.

clue.text: Having to lie about one's fight

indicators.note: about tells us one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to rest is to lie down
one is I, and 's stands for is, giving I'S

explanation.surface: A person has to tell untruths to win a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving I + S, which goes inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight against something, a synonym.

clue.text: Big tree specially trained to set by a highway

parts.note: a set or stand is a frame for holding things
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A large trained tree is placed beside a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just joins the pieces. A standard in gardening is a tree or shrub trained to grow on one tall bare stem.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners call a tree pruned to a single tall stem a standard.

clue.text: Records test that's material

parts.note: tapes are recordings, things recorded
to try is to test

explanation.surface: A judgement that recordings are worth testing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven fabric, a kind of textile.

clue.text: Dull colour can be both wise and unwise

parts.note: sage means wise
green means naive or inexperienced

explanation.surface: A paradox about a drab hue being wise and foolish at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be both' just links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage green is a soft greyish green shade, a muted hue.

clue.text: Looking around the civic centre feeling famished

indicators.note: around shows one piece placed so the other surrounds it

parts.note: staring is looking hard

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle letter of the word civic

explanation.surface: Someone wanders the town centre gazing about, desperately hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: To be starving is to feel extremely hungry.

clue.text: Animal circumventing snare in the dark

indicators.note: circumventing means going round, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a brute is a beast or animal
a net is a trap or snare

explanation.surface: A beast caught round a trap at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the dark' sounds like night, but 'the dark' is a dark-haired person.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette is a woman with dark hair, one of the dark-haired.

clue.text: Put out yet again about a matter of contention

parts.note: re means about, concerning
an issue is a point in dispute

explanation.surface: Something published once more on a disputed topic.
explanation.definitionFit: To reissue is to publish or release something a second time.

clue.text: Daughter men see managing the estate

indicators.note: managing suggests letters being handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter watches the men running the family estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land attached to a manor, an estate.

clue.text: The chairman in opposition never dithers

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: The chair of a meeting, facing opposition, is decisive.
explanation.definitionFit: A convener is the person who calls and chairs a meeting.

clue.text: The youngster guilty of pinching?

explanation.definitionFit: A small child is a nipper in British slang, and someone who nips pinches.

clue.text: A skilled technician is less likely to feel fatigue

definitions.meaning: a mechanic who assembles or installs parts

explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic who assembles machinery has this job title; also the comparative of fit, healthier.

clue.text: A point to be observed in the south or north

indicators.note: the letters can be seen inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A compass reading taken in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on a plant, a prickle.

clue.text: Told of being left cutting the long grass

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into another word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have been left to cut long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Reported means described or related, as told of.

clue.text: A European schoolboy can get round the school-head

indicators.note: get round tells us one piece wraps another

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil of Eton College
the head of the word school is its first letter, S

explanation.surface: A pupil from abroad manages to sweet-talk the headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the famous English boarding school; its pupils are Etonians.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Estonia is a European nationality.

clue.text: Go off every single player

parts.note: a stage direction telling all the actors to leave the stage

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction tells several performers to leave together.

clue.text: The adolescent generate chaos!

indicators.note: chaos suggests the letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A remark that young people create mayhem.
explanation.definitionFit: A young person aged thirteen to nineteen is an adolescent.
